# Appeal of Denied Prior Authorization — Request for Reconsideration

**RE:** Appeal of adverse benefit determination
**Member:** Jordan Alvarez
**Member ID:** W482428991
**Reference number:** POC-177B09D7A6-51151
**Date of denial notice:** August 11, 2026
**Service denied:** Neck (cervical) fusion (ACDF), CPT 22551
**Governing policy:** UnitedHealthcare Medical Policy, *Spinal Fusion and Decompression (2026T0639I)*, effective 2026-04-01 — https://www.uhcprovider.com/content/dam/provider/docs/public/policies/comm-medical-drug/spinal-fusion-decompression.pdf

**To:** UnitedHealthcare Appeals — [appeal address printed on my denial letter]

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for the cervical fusion (ACDF) surgery, CPT 22551, that my surgeon requested for me. The denial notice dated August 11, 2026 states that the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure. I am asking the plan to reconsider that decision. My surgeon has documented that this procedure is needed, and I believe the records already in the plan's possession line up with the plan's own published policy.

## What the plan's own policy says, and what my records show

The policy that governs this request, *Spinal Fusion and Decompression (2026T0639I)*, states:

> "Coverage Rationale Spinal procedures for the treatment of spine pain are proven and medically necessary in certain circumstances ."

The same policy also states:

> "Surgery may be an option for individuals whose pain cannot be controlled by more conservative methods (National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases, 2023)."

My records address both of these points directly.

**Conservative methods have been tried, and my pain has not been controlled.** The records submitted with the prior authorization document:

- 24 months of progressive neck pain, unrelieved by rest.
- Supervised physical therapy including cervical traction and postural training, 8 weeks from 2026-05-14 to 2026-07-09, with 18 visits completed. This is documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- NSAIDs for 4 months with inadequate relief.
- A corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-03, which gave 4 weeks of partial relief.

**The imaging identifies a specific structural cause, and my physical exam matches it.** On imaging dated 2026-06-04, MRI of the cervical spine showed a C5-C6 disc herniation with severe right foraminal narrowing and C6 nerve root compression. My symptoms and exam correspond to that finding: radicular pain and numbness into the right thumb and index finger with weakness, positive provocative testing on the affected side, and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level. The records also note that I have no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and that I am a non-smoker. My surgeon is Lindqvist, MD, orthopedic surgery.

In other words, the plan's policy contemplates surgery for people whose pain is not controlled by more conservative methods, and my chart documents both the failure of those methods and an imaging finding that corresponds to my examination at the same level the surgery is meant to treat.

I would also note two other things the policy says. It states:

> "Medical records documentation may be required to assess whether the member meets the clinical criteria for coverage but does not guarantee coverage of the service requested;"

I understand that. I am not asking for a guarantee — I am asking that the documentation actually be weighed against the criteria the plan applied. The policy also states:

> "For medical necessity clinical coverage criteria, refer to the:"

That sentence points to criteria that are not reproduced in the excerpt available to me, and the policy lists further conditions I have not seen. I am not in a position to argue against a standard I have never been shown. Where the plan has a specific threshold in mind — a required duration of treatment, a required finding, or a required imaging characteristic — the plan has not stated that threshold to me, and I am not quoting one, because none of the policy language I have identifies one. My argument is based on my own documented facts as they appear in the chart.

## Request for the criteria the plan applied

I am asking, in writing, for the specific rule or criterion relied on to deny this request. It is my understanding that reviews like mine may be conducted using InterQual, which is licensed software rather than a publicly available document, so I would not be able to look it up myself. I am therefore requesting, free of charge, **the InterQual subset, edition, and full criteria text applied to my determination**, along with the credentials of the reviewer who made this decision. If the denial was based on the imaging, please also state which imaging criterion my 2026-06-04 MRI was measured against and in what respect it was found not to meet that criterion.

## What I am asking for

I ask that UnitedHealthcare overturn the denial and authorize CPT 22551 as requested by Dr. Lindqvist. If the plan maintains the denial, I ask for a written explanation that identifies the exact criterion not met, cites the policy text containing it, and explains how that criterion was applied to my documented findings. I also ask that this letter be treated as a request for all appeal rights available to me, including external review.

My appeal must be received by **February 7, 2027**, per the denial notice. I am submitting this appeal through the member portal at **member.uhc.com**, and/or by mail to the appeal address printed on my denial letter. I understand I may also call the number on my member ID card about this appeal. There is no single public appeals fax or PO box, so I have used the address on my denial notice.

Thank you for taking a careful second look at this. I am glad to provide anything further that would help.

Sincerely,

**Jordan Alvarez**
